text:
The Canadiens went out and got Dylan Larkin, and the hockey since has not cooperated. Montreal is winless in three, outscored 12-4, and the last stop was a 6-0 loss in Colorado where Mackenzie Blackwood saw 28 shots and stopped every one. Our read is that the slide is partly real: the Canadiens had 46% of the expected goals (the quality of their chances) across those three games. Larkin, the former Red Wings captain who forced his way out of Detroit, has already moved onto the first power-play unit, and Arpon Basu of The Athletic posted Friday's practice lines in Vegas with Ivan Demidov back beside Nick Suzuki and Alex Newhook. ESPN still lists Demidov on injured reserve with an estimated return of Nov. 30, so watch the warmups. Kaiden Guhle and Mike Matheson are still out, and Chris Kreider is on IR until January.

Vegas played last night and it showed. The Sharks beat the Golden Knights 4-1 in San Jose, and Vegas managed only 37% of the expected goals, its worst night in a stretch where it had won the chance battle in four straight games. Now it is the second night of a back-to-back, which our numbers account for. Jack Eichel carries a six-game point streak into it, and Trevor Connelly, who leads all rookies in points according to The Athletic's Jesse Granger, has given Ryan Craig's team a new source of offense.

The goaltending matchup is upside down from last season. Jakub Dobes, who saved 17 goals above expected a year ago, starts over Jacob Fowler and sits at an .868 save rate and 3.6 goals below expected. Adin Hill was 15 below expected last season and is above water now, 2-0-3 with 3.8 saved above expected over his last five starts.

Juraj Slafkovský is the Montreal name we keep circling: no goals in 17 games on 5.3 expected goals, and two points from 200 for his career. Montreal also takes 4.7 penalties a game, which is a lot of time to spend killing against a Vegas power play that makes 0.81 expected goals a game.
headline: Larkin's Canadiens arrive in Vegas still searching
